title: P02 extension: optimize the output readout (head.weight) with Muon instead of AdamW
description: P02 (Muon): move the untied 99x256 output readout head.weight from pretraining AdamW into the existing split-QKV Muon group (same LR 0.01 schedule, momentum, decay), leaving embeddings/biases/LayerNorms on AdamW and everything else as 051-claude. Muon's orthogonalized updates were the single largest downstream gain in this loop, and an orthogonalized readout update moves all 99 output-token directions at equal spectral magnitude, which should keep rare tokens (high line-index citations reached mainly through the ref-shift augmentation, and long-proof continuations) from being under-trained relative to frequent ones, giving expert iteration a broader, better-calibrated sampling distribution on >=7-line targets.
hypothesis: Under AdamW the readout's updates are dominated by frequent tokens and its singular spectrum becomes low-rank/peaky; Muon equalizes the update across output directions, so the logit geometry for rare citation tokens and long-proof continuations is better formed at handoff. That should raise round-1 sample accuracy on >=7-line targets and compound through the four EI rounds. Counter-risk: Keller Jordan reports Muon on the output layer is worse for LM loss at scale, so val loss may rise slightly; the downstream metric decides.
expected_delta: -30 to +20 theorems at >=7 (central ~-5); val loss within +-0.003 of 051; steps within 3% of 051 (one extra 99x256 Newton-Schulz per step)

arch.change: none versus 051-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices AND the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction; head.weight therefore keeps the same per-step multiplicative decay it had under AdamW.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 051: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. No init change in this experiment; per-seed initial weights and data order bitwise identical to 051.
